sentences.text: Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3. The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of respondent No.2, the police registered the FIR and it is alleged by the complainant that she got married with petitioner No.1 on 29.06.2020.
At the time of marriage, her mother has given dowry of Rs.2,00,000/- cash, golden ring, chain, watch and 20 pairs of cloths, almirah, cot, washing machine etc., and all house hold items.
Subsequent to the marriage, the accused NC: 2024:KHC:10097 persons said to be demanded additional dowry and a motor bike for accused No.1 and unnecessarily, they troubled her physically and mentally.

Hence,
she filed a complaint.
After registering the FIR, the Police investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that there is omnibus allegation against all the petitioners which is the general allegation.
There is no specific allegation for demanding any dowry etc.
The petitioner No.1 filed the divorce case against the respondent No.2 on 31.03.2021.

Subsequently, complaint came to be filed after one year 4 months of leaving the house and there is no prima facie material against the petitioners and hence, prayed for quashing the criminal proceedings.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 objected the petition and contended that there is prima facie material placed on record against the petitioners for having committed the offence and learned High Court Government Pleader also submits that there is prima facie material for NC:
2024:KHC:10097 having committed the offence.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the petition.

6. Having heard the arguments and perused the records, on perusal of the complaint as well as the charge sheet material, there are three eye witnesses and neighbours were examined by the Investigating Officer other than the mother of the complainant but they have stated about the dowry, receipt of dowry articles and also other utensils, demand of dowry and assaulting the complainant by the petitioners.
However, the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 is the mother-in-law.
The other petitioners are brother, sister and brother in laws were all married and residing separately.
The allegation is also common and genuine in nature.
Except the allegation against accused Nos.1 and 2 who are husband and mother in law of respondent No.2, the other allegations are common and general in nature.
In the similar case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Others vs. State of Bihar & Others reported in 2022 LiveLa w (SC) 141, has quashed the criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Others vs. State of Bihar & Others reported in 2022 LiveLa w (SC) 141
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Except accused Nos.1 and 2, the remaining accused are in laws of respondent No.2 and most of them were residing separately not NC: 2024:KHC:10097 in the house of accused Nos.1 and 2.
Such being the case, the question of framing of charge against the petitioners does not arise.
Of course, accused Nos.1 and 2 are husband and mother- in-law of respondent No.2, they stayed together in the matrimonial house along with the complainant.
Such being the case, I am of the view, the petition filed by accused Nos.1 and 2 is required to be dismissed and the petition filed by accused Nos.3 to 10 is liable to be allowed.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed in part.
The petition filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.3 to 10 is hereby allowed.
